questions.q: What does a depolarizing error with probability p do to a gate's output?
options: It always flips the qubit's bit value
With probability (1-p) the gate behaves ideally; with probability p its output is replaced with a fully random, maximally mixed result
It slows down the simulation but never changes the result
It only affects measurement, never gates
questions.explain: Depolarizing noise follows the channel rho -> (1-p)*rho + p*I/4 for a 2-qubit gate: with probability p, the correct operation is replaced entirely by a maximally mixed (random) result.

questions.q: Which Qiskit Aer call builds a 1% depolarizing error for a 2-qubit gate?
options: `NoiseModel(0.01)`
`depolarizing_error(0.01, 2)`
`AerSimulator(noise=0.01)`
`add_all_qubit_quantum_error(0.01)`
questions.explain: `depolarizing_error(p, n)` builds the error channel itself, specifying probability p and the number of qubits n the gate acts on; it's then attached to a NoiseModel with `add_all_qubit_quantum_error`.

questions.q: With a noiseless Bell-state circuit, P(01) and P(10) are exactly 0. With a 1% depolarizing error on the CX gate, what do the exact calculations give for these probabilities?
options: They stay exactly 0
They become 0.25 each
They become 0.0025 each — small but genuinely nonzero
They become 0.5 each
questions.explain: The exact depolarizing-channel calculation gives P(01)=P(10)=0.0025 under 1% CX depolarizing error, versus P(00)=P(11)=0.4975 -- noise opens up outcomes that were exactly impossible in the ideal circuit.

questions.q: A real seeded run of the noisy Bell-state circuit at shots=4096 gave `{'00': 2090, '01': 11, '10': 8, '11': 1987}`. What is the diagnostic significance of the nonzero `01` and `10` counts?
options: They are a sign of a coding mistake in the circuit
They are the expected signature of real gate error, since these outcomes are exactly impossible in the noiseless ideal circuit
They mean more shots must be run before the results mean anything
They indicate the simulator ignored the noise model
questions.explain: Because P(01) and P(10) are exactly 0 under the noiseless circuit, any nonzero occurrence of these outcomes is attributable to the modeled gate error, not to ordinary sampling noise on an already-possible outcome.

Attaches the given error channel to every `cx` gate in the circuit across all qubit pairs
Attaches the error only to the first cx gate in the circuit
Applies the error to measurement operations only
questions.explain: This NoiseModel method attaches the specified quantum error to the named gate (here `cx`) uniformly across all qubits in the circuit, so every CX gate run on this backend inherits the error.
